text:
Maya Patel: Heads up — seeing ALB target group evicting a subset of edge-gpu nodes in us-west-2. Pods show Ready in k8s but target group flips to Unhealthy after a few checks. Not tied to pod restarts, looks correlated with TLS handshakes.

Rajiv Chen: Any envoy logs? Did something change on the mesh or TLS inspector configs?

Maya Patel: Found this in envoy sidecar logs around the timestamps when ALB marks unhealthy: 
```
[warning] tls_inspector: no SNI found, no matching filter chain, closing connection
[info] http_connection_manager: downstream connection closed before request complete
```
ALB health checks are HTTPS. I think ALB isn't sending SNI (or Host) on its health check TLS handshake.

Leo SRE: Interesting. ALB health checks historically do not set SNI unless you override the Host header on the target group health check. If envoy relies on SNI for filter chain selection, empty SNI -> no filter -> connection closed -> ALB sees connection failure -> marks unhealthy.

Maya Patel: That would explain why k8s thinks the pod is fine (readiness probe is HTTP inside pod) but ALB sees TLS-level failure. Also this only started after we rolled the new envoy config that uses SNI-based filter chains for routing GPUs to the edge-vhost.

Rajiv Chen: Quick check: what does the target group health check look like? I see in terraform we had: 
```
health_check {
  protocol = "HTTPS"
  path     = "/healthz"
  port     = "traffic-port"
  // no host override
}
```
No host override -> ALB will not set SNI.

Leo SRE: Two remediation paths: 1) set host override on the TG health check to the vhost so ALB will send SNI/Host; 2) add a default filter chain in envoy that accepts empty SNI and routes to health handler. Which do we prefer short-term?

Maya Patel: Short term I'd rather change TG health check to include Host override (less code change). I'll patch the TF and reapply to the affected TGs for the edge-gpu pool.

infra-bot: Apply queued: terraform plan for aws_lb_target_group.edge-gpu-tg (will update health_check.host)

Rajiv Chen: Also add an envoy fallback so we don't regress on future deploys that expect SNI. Put a comment in the mesh config explaining the dependency.

Maya Patel: Patch applied, TG health check Host set to `edge-api.redwood.internal`. Watching...

Leo SRE: ALB reports targets healthy again for the two previously evicted targets. K8s readiness unchanged. Looks like fix worked, will let this bake for a bit.

Maya Patel: Confirmed — targets back to healthy across the pool. Leaving a follow-up ticket to add envoy default filter chain and a canary to ensure health-check SNI assumptions are documented. :thumbsup:

Rajiv Chen: Nice catch. Logging the root cause: envoy uses SNI-only filter chains; ALB health checks over TLS do not include SNI/Host unless host override configured -> intermittent TLS-level closes -> target deregistration.

Leo SRE: TL;DR: If you use SNI-based routing in sidecars, make sure LB health checks include the Host override or accept empty SNI in the filter chain.

Maya Patel: Adding ticket: INFRA-3241 (envoy fallback + doc)
